headline: Scimitar-horned oryx returns from extinction
meta_description: A species declared extinct in the wild now thrives again. More than 600 scimitar-horned oryx live wild in Chad after conservationists began reintroduction in 2…
summary_short: The scimitar-horned oryx, once extinct in the wild, has made a remarkable comeback. More than 600 animals now live in Chad's Ouadi Rimé-Ouadi Achim reserve.
body:
The scimitar-horned oryx has returned from extinction in the wild. More than 600 of the animals now live wild in Chad, a stunning reversal for a species that had vanished entirely from its native range across North Africa.

In 2016, conservationists began reintroducing captive-bred oryx to Chad's Ouadi Rimé-Ouadi Achim Faunal Reserve, starting with just 23 animals. The population has grown steadily since that modest beginning, proving that careful restoration can work even for species at the brink.

The progress earned recognition in 2023, when the International Union for Conservation of Nature downlisted the scimitar-horned oryx from Extinct in the Wild to Endangered—an official acknowledgment that dedicated reintroduction efforts can bring species back from the edge.

Reintroduction began in 2016 with just 23 animals
Located in Ouadi Rimé-Ouadi Achim Faunal Reserve
